To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
wheat gliadin enhances IL-4-induced production of IgE in normal human peripheral blood mononucler cells through a red-ox dependent mechanism.
the wheat gliadin promotes IgE production by the human peripheral blood monocyte cells through a red-ox dependent mechanism.
gliadin, a protein found in wheat and other cereal grains, promotes the production of IgE in normal human peripheral monocytes, a process that could be counteracted in vitro by natural antioxidants.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the biological mechanisms of the gliadin-induced allergy.
the identification of the molecular mechanisms involved in the gliadin-induced IgE production.
the possible involvement of gliadin in the IgE production and in the redox balance in normal human PBMC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
gliadin promotes the IgE production in normal human PBMC by an oxidative mechanism.
gliadin is able to enhance the IgE production by PBMC in a redox-dependent manner.
gliadin promotes the IL-4 induced IgE production by peripheral mononuclear human cells through a red-ox-dependent mechanism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
gliadins promote IgE production through a redox mechanism, and that this IgE production could be suppressed by thiols and/or by vectorized SOD.
gliadin could be involved in the IgE production through the regulation of the redox balance in human PBMC, and that the antioxidant treatment could counteract this pro-allergenic effect.
wheat gliadin is able to promote the IgE production by PBMC in vitro through a redox mechanism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
gliadins, which are the main allergenic proteins in wheat, can promote the IgE production by PBMC through redox imbalance.
wheat gliadin promotes the production of IgE, which is a hallmark of allergy, through a redox dependent mechanism.
wheat gliadin promotes the IL-4-mediated IgE production by peripheral blood mononucleocytes through a redox dependent pathway.
